subject: QuantumHealth — Renewal insights, burst capacity pilot & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@quantumhealth.io>, Asha Rao <asha.rao@quantumhealth.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: renewal context + recommended pilot (usage attached)

Hi Jordan / Asha —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re all aligned and to capture next steps. I tried to keep this tight — happy to expand any section.

Summary of what we heard
- Primary business driver: stabilize response latency and cost during end-of-business (EOB) batch processing windows for your claims-rerank workflow.
- Current usage: ~350M tokens / month (peak daily burst ~18M tokens), embeddings on ~2M vectors/day for RAG.
- Pain points: intermittent tail latency (200–700ms spikes), rising per-token spend as retrievals scale, and stricter audit/retention requirements for PHI-derived prompts.
- Stakeholders: Jordan (product), Asha (infra/security), Procurement (procurement@quantumhealth.io).

Recommendation (short): 6-week burst-capacity pilot on Redwood Dedicated + prefix/KV caching for RAG. Goals: reduce tail latency to <120ms p50/p95, cut effective token cost by 30% via caching + batching, and validate SOC-compliant telemetry into your audit pipeline.

What I attached
- usage_report_QH-Nov2026.csv (breakdown by model, seq length, peak days)
- security_slide_deck.pdf (SOC2 outline, KMS options)

Immediate asks / proposed next steps
1) Confirm pilot scope & acceptance criteria (latency target, cost target, retention window) — Jordan/Asha by Thu 12/3
2) Procurement contact + PO timing — procurement@quantumhealth.io by Fri 12/10
3) If agreed, we’ll share a draft SOW and pricing estimate (turnaround 48 hours).

Proposed timeline (if greenlit)
- 12/13: SOW signed (DocuSign)
- 12/20: Technical kickoff & access provisioning
- 12/21–1/31: Pilot execution (6 weeks)
- 2/3: Pilot review and go/no-go for renewal/scale

If this matches your notes, I’ll loop in Marissa (CS) to scope onboarding tasks.

Thanks —
Ben

Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@quantumhealth.io>

Cc: Asha Rao <asha.rao@quantumhealth.io>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: renewal context + recommended pilot (usage attached)

Ben —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirmed pain points: the biggest user-impact is the latency spikes during the nightly reconciliation window (18:00–20:00 ET). Those spikes cause timeouts in our downstream batch jobs and backfill work.
- Embeddings cost is the other leaky bucket; we already pre-filter queries but we’re seeing vector store I/O contribute to 40% of the spend on some days.
- Compliance: we need to make sure KV/prefix caching can be scoped so PHI tokens are not retained beyond the retention policy; SOC2 artifacts will be required for review.

Questions:
1) For the proposed dedicated-burst pool: what’s the shortest lead time to provision for a pilot (we prefer <2 weeks)?
2) Ballpark pilot cost for 6 weeks (we’re looking for an order-of-magnitude for budgetary approval).

I’ll confirm procurement contact (looping them in next). If you can include Marissa and Monica in the SOW conversation that’d be great.

—Jordan
Jordan Ellis | Director, Product
QuantumHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@quantumhealth.io>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Asha Rao <asha.rao@quantumhealth.io>
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 11:46:00 -0800
Subject: Proposed pilot scope & SOW draft (attached)

Jordan / Asha —

Looping in as requested. I attached a short SOW (proposed_sow_dedicated-burst.pdf) with the pilot scope and an initial pricing estimate. High level:

Pilot scope (6 weeks)
- Dedicated burst pool: reserved capacity for 2x your current peak (supporting ~36M tokens/day peak) with automated fallback to hosted for overflow.
- RAG optimizations: prefix/KV caching enabled for non-PHI traffic, quantized model variant for async embedding batch jobs, and batching policy tuned to match your seq-length distribution.
- Observability: token-level trace for sampled requests, latency p50/p95 dashboards, and audit log export to your S3 (KMS integration).

Acceptance criteria
- p95 latency reduction vs current baseline by >= 35% during EOB windows OR p95 < 200ms (whichever is met first).
- Effective token cost reduction >= 25% vs current configuration measured over 2 consecutive sample weeks.
- Successful export of audit logs to your S3 with encryption keys managed by your KMS.

Ballpark pricing
- Pilot fixed setup: $6,000 (one-time) — covers provisioning, security review, and onboarding.
- Pilot run: ~$18k–24k for 6 weeks depending on actual peak usage (we’ll reconcile final usage after pilot).

Attachments and next steps
- Attached: proposed_sow_dedicated-burst.pdf (SOW + terms)
- Security annex is summarized in security_slide_deck.pdf (shared earlier).

Action items
- Jordan / Asha: confirm acceptance criteria + procurement timeline by Fri 12/10
- Procurement: review SOW and confirm PO timing — procurement@quantumhealth.io
- Redwood (Marissa/Monica/Ben): we’ll finalize SOW and send DocuSign once procurement confirms.

If those numbers look reasonable I’ll get the SOW on DocuSign as the next step.

Thanks —
Marissa
